response:
Honestly, there's nothing wrong with being "normal"—and starting your own group could be a great way to connect with people who don't feel like they fit neatly into a box. Chances are, plenty of others feel exactly like you do: stuck between cliques, not wanting to force themselves into a label just to belong somewhere.

The good news is that friendships don't have to come from a pre-made group. Sometimes the best connections start one person at a time—someone you sit next to in class, or another new student still finding their footing. You don't have to become a theater kid or anything else just to have people around you. Give it a little time; new schools feel overwhelming at first, but you'll find your people. And if "The Normal Ones" ends up being real, that sounds like a pretty welcoming club to be part of.
